t: The comprehensive motor policy covering own damage was first introduced in England in
e: Own damage (comprehensive) cover appeared in 1899, four years after the first TP-only policy of 1895.

t: The India Motor Tariff presently followed came into existence with effect from
e: The new Motor Tariff with 49 General Regulations took effect on 1 July 2002 and its structure continues even after detariffing.

t: Add-on covers under motor policies may be offered by insurers
o: Under IRDAI's file and use provisions
Only as part of the tariff wordings
e: Post detariffing, insurers can provide add-on covers approved by IRDAI under file and use guidelines; the standard policy wordings continue.

t: In double insurance of a motor vehicle, the principle of contribution requires the loss to be shared
e: Contribution applies in double insurance: each insurer bears a ratable proportion of the compensation, costs or expenses.

t: A licence for a non-transport vehicle issued to a 28 year old driver remains effective until
e: Where the driver is below 30 at issue, the licence is valid till the date he attains 40 years.

t: An endorsement to carry dangerous or hazardous goods is valid for
e: The hazardous goods endorsement is valid for 3 years, requires age 20, medical fitness, a transport licence and knowledge of English plus one Schedule VII language.

t: Under Section 25A, a driving licence issued or renewed is not valid unless it carries a unique number under the
e: The 2019 amendment created a National Register of Driving Licences maintained by the Central Government, subsuming State registers.

t: If a vehicle owner changes his residential address, he must intimate the new address to the RTO within
e: The owner must intimate change of address within 30 days of the change; the RC remains valid throughout India.

t: Under Section 41, in the case of a new vehicle the application for registration in the same State is to be made by
e: The dealer applies for registration of a new vehicle in the same State and must not deliver it until the registration mark is displayed.

t: A transport vehicle driving licence issued under Section 10 remains valid for
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Transport vehicle licences are valid for 5 years; the age-linked durations apply to non-transport classes.

t: Under Section 54, registration suspended under Section 53 may be cancelled if the suspension continues uninterrupted for not less than
e: Cancellation follows when suspension for being unroadworthy or dangerous continues for at least six months.

t: Under Section 81, an application for renewal of a permit must be made not less than
e: Permits (other than temporary) are valid for five years and renewal must be applied for at least 15 days before expiry.

t: 'Aggregator' under Section 2(1A) of the amended MV Act means
o: A transport company owning more than 50 vehicles
A digital intermediary connecting passengers with drivers
e: The 2019 amendment defined aggregator as a digital intermediary or marketplace for passengers to connect with drivers, enabling app-based operators.

t: Section 128(3) requires a motorcycle carrying a child aged between nine months and four years as pillion to be driven at a speed not exceeding
e: Safety harness, crash helmet and a speed limit of 40 km/h apply when carrying a child of 9 months to 4 years.

t: Under Section 134, after an accident causing injury the driver must inform the nearest police station within
e: The driver must take the injured to hospital, inform the police within 24 hours and inform the insurer with policy and driver particulars.

t: A Good Samaritan under Section 134A is protected from civil or criminal liability when he
o: Renders emergency care or transports the victim in good faith without expectation of reward
Drives the injured person's vehicle to the police station
Pays compensation on behalf of the driver
e: Section 134A shields persons who voluntarily and without reward render emergency medical or non-medical assistance or transport the victim to hospital.

t: The arbitration condition of a motor policy applies to disputes regarding
e: Arbitration is available only where the dispute is on the amount payable and not where liability itself is denied.

t: Own damage premium is ₹12,000 and the insured has completed four consecutive claim-free years. The NCB amount is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). NCB after 4 completed claim-free years is 45%; 45% of ₹12,000 is ₹6,600.

t: An insured settles with a third party and admits liability without consulting the insurer. This breaches the condition relating to
o: No admission, offer, promise or payment
e: The insured cannot make any admission, offer, promise or payment without the insurer's prior written consent.

t: Which of the following is a general exclusion applicable to all sections of the motor policy?
o: Loss of accessories not on the vehicle
e: General exclusions cover loss outside the geographical area, contractual liability, breach of limitations as to use or driver clause, consequential loss and war/nuclear risks.

t: Section III (towing of a disabled vehicle) under a commercial vehicle policy provides
o: Liability cover while towing a disabled vehicle not for hire or reward
OD cover for the towed vehicle
Cover for goods carried in the towed vehicle
e: Section III extends Section II liability cover to a mechanically disabled towed vehicle, not for reward, with no OD cover for the towed vehicle or its load.

t: With effect from 30.03.2012, which miscellaneous vehicle was reclassified to be rated as a goods carrying commercial vehicle?
e: Dumpers, tippers, milk vans, tankers, oil transport vehicles, refrigeration units and goods carrying tractors were moved from Class D to GCCV rating under Section 4A.

t: Mobile cranes and excavators can be covered for damage by overturning during operational use under IMT-47 at an additional premium of
e: IMT-47 extends package policies for mobile units to overturning as a tool of trade at 0.5% of IDV.

t: A car's IDV is ₹5,00,000 and the wreck fetches ₹80,000 on an 'as is where is' basis. The maximum insurer liability on a total loss basis where the insured retains the wreck is
e: Insurer's liability cannot exceed IDV less the value of the wreck, i.e. ₹4,20,000 before policy deductibles.

t: The IDV depreciation schedule applies what percentage for a vehicle aged above 6 months but not exceeding 1 year?
e: IDV depreciation is 5% below 6 months, 15% for 6 months to 1 year, 20%, 30%, 40% and 50% for subsequent years up to 5 years.

t: Plastic bumper ₹6,000, airbag ₹30,000 and metal door ₹20,000 are replaced on a car aged 2 years 4 months. Total depreciation is
e: Plastic and airbag attract 50% (₹3,000 + ₹15,000); the metal door at 2-3 years attracts 15% (₹3,000); total ₹21,000.

t: Under GR-12, the short period premium for a cover up to one month is
e: The short period scale starts at 20% of annual premium for up to one month and reaches full premium above 8 months.

t: A private car of 1800 cc has an assessed OD loss of ₹25,000 after depreciation. The amount payable after compulsory deductible is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR-40 compulsory deductible for private cars exceeding 1500 cc is ₹2,000, so ₹23,000 is payable.

t: Under GR-25, the fee for each issuance of a fresh certificate of insurance on change in the policy is
e: ₹50 is charged for every fresh certificate of insurance, and the old certificate is to be surrendered.

t: Under GR-26, when a certificate of insurance is lost, the fresh certificate issued is to be
o: Marked 'duplicate' after obtaining a declaration on circumstances of loss
e: A declaration with full particulars of loss and efforts made is taken, the fresh certificate is marked duplicate and the original returned if found.

t: A bank requires the earlier-dated of two policies on a financed car to be cancelled. The refund is
o: On short period scale for the period in force
e: Where the earlier policy is cancelled at the written requirement of a financial institution, premium is retained on short period scale and the balance refunded.

t: The NCB percentage for one completed claim-free year is
e: NCB runs 20%, 25%, 35%, 45% and 50% for one to five consecutive claim-free years.

t: NCB earned on a vehicle insured abroad can be allowed in India if claimed within
e: NCB is applicable worldwide; NCB earned abroad can be allowed within 3 years of the expiry date and vice versa.

t: Where an insured gives an NCB declaration that later proves false, the consequence stated in the declaration wording is
o: Benefits under Section I (OD) are forfeited
e: The declaration provides that if found incorrect, all benefits under Section I of the policy stand forfeited.

t: An insured opts for a voluntary deductible of ₹15,000 on a car with OD premium of ₹9,000. The discount allowed is
e: ₹15,000 voluntary deductible gives 35% (₹3,150) subject to a maximum of ₹2,500, so ₹2,500 applies.

t: Vehicles imported without customs duty by embassies, where the duty element is not in the IDV, attract
e: GR-37 (IMT-19) loads OD premium by 30% where import duty is not included in the IDV.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

t: Optional PA cover for unnamed passengers in a private car is limited to
o: The registered carrying capacity of the vehicle
e: Unnamed passenger PA cover is limited to the registered carrying capacity, excluding the insured, paid driver and cleaner, with CSI up to ₹2 lakh per person.

t: The compulsory deductible applicable to a passenger carrying vehicle with 40 seats is
e: PCVs above 36 passengers carry ₹1,500; 17 to 36 passengers ₹1,000; below 17 passengers ₹500.

t: Under GR-43, the extra OD premium for a fibre glass fuel tank on a Class D commercial vehicle is
e: GR-43 charges ₹100 for Class D vehicles and ₹50 for all other vehicles.

t: Constructive total loss mode is generally adopted when
o: IDV is higher than market value
The vehicle is less than one year old
IDV less salvage is lower than the repair liability
e: CTL is adopted when retrieval cost is 75% or more and IDV less salvage is lower than the repair liability, making total-loss settlement in the insurer's interest.

t: Under the regulations summarised by the trainer, the surveyor must submit his interim report within
e: Interim report within 15 days of first visit, final report within 30 days, and within 90 days for commercial vehicle and large risk claims.

t: The insurer must furnish a free copy of the proposal form to the insured within
e: A copy of the proposal must be supplied free of charge within 30 days of acceptance of the proposal.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: Premium under a Motor Trade Transit Risk (Class E) policy is charged on the basis of
e: Class E covers vehicles driven under their own power from manufacturer's warehouse to showroom and is rated on distance.

t: Under Section 157, on transfer of ownership the new owner must apply to the insurer for transfer of the policy within
e: Section 157 deems the liability portion transferred from the date of transfer and requires the transferee to apply within 14 days.

t: Section 164 (earlier 163A) compensation for grievous hurt without proof of fault is
e: Section 164 provides ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt; the claimant need not establish negligence.

t: A copy of the MACT award is to be given to the parties within
e: Section 168: copy of award within 15 days and the award to be satisfied within 30 days from the date of award.

t: Jald Rahat Yojana covers
o: Only cases pending in High Court
Non-fatal injury cases excluding hit-and-run, for claimants above 18 years
e: JRY (14.03.1992) is a pre-litigation scheme for non-fatal injury cases, fault and no-fault, excluding hit and run, for claimants above 18.

t: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, the pecuniary jurisdiction of the District Commission extends to claims up to
e: District Commission up to ₹1 crore, State Commission above ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore and National Commission above ₹10 crore.
